scope: Acceptance requirements; not a claim that real Oracle or cross-backend tests have run

cases.description: Existing valid refresh Cookie succeeds without body, with the expected envelope, two matching HttpOnly cookies and unchanged session identity.
Without a nonempty Cookie, a valid JSON or URL-encoded form body token succeeds; an expired access Cookie must not block this public endpoint.
An invalid nonempty refresh Cookie takes precedence over a valid body; a nonempty whitespace-only Cookie does not fall back to the body.
With normal database connection and close, absent, non-string, unparseable, expired and wrong-signature credentials return 401 with no new cookie and no session mutation.
Incorrect user, session or stored refresh hash, revoked and expired database sessions do not rotate.
A successful rotation invalidates old access and refresh credentials; a second same-second rotation creates a distinct refresh token.
With normal database and network behavior, concurrent use of one old refresh token has exactly one successful conditional update and one failed response without cookies.
Database failures return a safe error and no new cookies; an unknown commit outcome is not represented as a guaranteed rollback.
CORS preflight is handled before authentication and does not query the session store.

With shared signing keys, each backend accepts and rotates tokens issued by each backend against one isolated Oracle database; Web and Flutter complete refresh and a subsequent supported protected request using their configured backend.
